subject.title: [Security] Unsafe deserialization of incoming WebSocket commands in Gateway

question: Does any validated Gateway request path copy parsed attacker-controlled properties into a prototype-bearing object, warranting parser-level or dispatcher-level rejection of prototype keys?
rationale: The issue concerns a protected security boundary, but the proposed fix assumes a Zod parser architecture that current main does not use and no exploitable source-to-sink path has been shown.

options.title: Audit then disposition
options.body: Privately trace the current parse, validation, and method-dispatch paths and close as unsubstantiated if no mutation sink is reachable; otherwise land a focused regression-backed fix.

options.title: Defensive parser rejection
options.body: Reject restricted prototype keys at the shared frame-parsing boundary, accepting the resulting protocol compatibility change as defense in depth.

options.title: Method-level hardening
options.body: Keep JSON parsing unchanged and harden only concrete merge or assignment sinks found in individual request handlers.

recommendation.title: Audit then disposition
recommendation.body: Privately trace the current parse, validation, and method-dispatch paths and close as unsubstantiated if no mutation sink is reachable; otherwise land a focused regression-backed fix.
